cp.name: Access request approved
cp.what: OIG request requires manager approval before any grant is executed — the deny-by-default gate.
cp.el: Okta OIG request object: requester, approver, target, timestamps
cp.ev: Population export of all OIG requests · hash raw response
cp.ca: Two-source reconciliation: OIG requests vs. GitHub grant events
cp.gap: Approver ≠ requester enforced in policy config — evidence the config, not just the tickets.

cp.name: Grant matches approval
cp.what: Provisioning bot executes exactly the approved scope — grant compared to request, deltas flagged.
cp.el: Bot execution log: approved scope vs. granted scope
cp.gap: The bot is a trusted actor — its own service account and code path need CM controls (see CM lane).

cp.name: Time-bound · auto-revoke
cp.what: Grant carries an expiry; revocation fires without human action. The control is the configuration.
cp.ca: Hash raw config · alert if TTL policy absent

name: Change management — code to production
sub: the path to prod is the control surface

cp.name: Branch protection · SoD
cp.what: Approver ≠ author required before merge; enforced by ruleset, not by process.
cp.el: Branch protection ruleset per in-scope repo
cp.ev: Config snapshot per repo, hashed, diffed daily
cp.ca: Population = in-scope repo list from product mapping; drift alerts
cp.gap: Admin bypass is the residual — evidence the bypass log and the org-level allowance.

cp.name: Required checks pass
cp.what: Security + functional CI checks are required statuses — a failed check mechanically blocks merge.
cp.el: Required status checks config + check-run results
cp.ca: Hash raw responses · classify checks security vs functional

cp.name: Apply bound to reviewed commit
cp.what: Terraform applies only from the merged commit via the pipeline — execution moved off laptops, credentials centralized, provenance preserved.
cp.el: Pipeline run: source SHA vs. applied SHA
cp.api: Actions run log + Terraform plan/apply record
cp.ca: Reconcile applied SHA to merged PR population
cp.gap: The value here is provenance and separation of duties — not cryptographic integrity in transit. Say it that way.

cp.name: Drift detection
cp.what: Live state vs. IaC state compared on schedule; out-of-band change surfaces as an alert, not at audit.
cp.el: CAI live state vs. Terraform state delta
cp.api: Cloud Asset Inventory export + state file compare
cp.ev: Delta report per run · alert population
cp.ca: Two-source: live inventory vs. declared state

cp.name: Term feed completeness
cp.what: Every termination in the HRIS appears in the deprovisioning queue — the population control everything downstream depends on.
cp.el: Termination feed: worker, type, term date
cp.ev: Population export · row-count reconciliation vs. HR report
cp.gap: Contractors and collaborators often live outside the HRIS — that population needs its own source.

cp.name: Revoked ≤ 5 business days
cp.what: Deprovision timestamp vs. termination date, tested across the full population — no sampling.
cp.el: Deactivation events joined to term feed

cp.name: Downstream revocation verified
cp.what: SSO revocation ≠ local account revocation — verify per system where local accounts exist.
cp.el: Per-system account status for terminated users
cp.ev: Log query per system · exceptions to review
cp.gap: This is where most programs quietly fail — SCIM coverage map determines which systems need it.
